quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A motorcycle needs _____ attention than a car.

options.text: Less
The same amount of
More

questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more attention than cars. You must check your motorcycle before riding. Problems that seem small can be dangerous at high speeds.

questions.question: Which lane position lets a car driver see you in their rearview mirror?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
No lane position allows you to be seen

questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This position usually appears in the rearview mirror of the car ahead. Most drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in emergencies
Should be used with the rear brake
Is unsafe to use

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used with the rear brake
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters
Blue with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Give you an escape route
Help you get hit by wind blasts
Show other drivers what you plan to do

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you get hit by wind blasts
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should prevent other riders from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: The mirrors show everything around you
The mirrors have blind spots
Do not use the mirrors except when parking

questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: The gearshift is located:

options.text: By the left footrest
By the right footrest
By the right handle grip

questions.explanation: The gearshift is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay within the speed limit
Go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass
Pass more than one vehicle at once

questions.explanation: Complete all passes within the legal speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes you easier to see
Speed up to cross quickly
Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster

questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, position yourself to be most visible. Cover the clutch and both brakes to reduce your reaction time. Slow down as you approach. Do not change your speed or position suddenly, as this can confuse other drivers.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves on rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross faster
Make bigger zigzags to get other drivers' attention
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on grooves or gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight. Do not try to zigzag, as this is more dangerous and keeps you from staying in your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns drivers that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: For motorcycle operators, helmets are:

options.text: Required.
Not required, but recommended.
Not recommended.

questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet whenever you operate a motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a potential problem?

options.text: An upcoming change in road surface characteristics
Surrounding traffic
Conditions that do not appear to change as you approach

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that do not appear to change as you approach
questions.explanation: Watch for hazards on the road and make a plan to reduce the risk they create.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Allow you to blend in with traffic.
Provide an escape route.
Encourage others to use your lane.

questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should keep other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If you are passing parked vehicles on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked vehicles and there is no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid opening car doors and pedestrians stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Use your mirrors. You do not need to look over your shoulder unless you notice something unusual.
Either use your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no other drivers are in your way.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your desired direction.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections
On the highway
On any road

questions.explanation: The greatest danger for motorcyclists happens at intersections. Cars turning left in front of motorcycles cause the most accidents.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Adjust your lane position in curves to see better and be seen better. In a left curve, ride right to spot oncoming traffic early. In a right curve, ride left-center to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If you need to react to a hazard in the road, do not:

options.text: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
Adjust your speed accordingly.
Make your presence known by sounding your horn and/or using lights or signals.

questions.explanation: Tell other drivers about your presence using your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed and lane position as needed to handle the hazard safely.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you arrive at the same time as another vehicle. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while riding over bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the gratings faster.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Zigzagging to stay in your lane is dangerous.

questions.question: _________ of crashes between motorcycles and cars are caused by the car driver not yielding to the motorcycle.

options.text: One-quarter
More than half
One-half

questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because drivers fail to yield to motorcyclists. Never assume a larger vehicle will yield, even if required by law.

questions.question: Why shouldn't a motorcyclist rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.
Mirrors are always unreliable.
Motorcycles have blind spots.

questions.explanation: Mirrors alone are not enough to see everything around you. Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle.

questions.question: When stopping at a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Skip the stop sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop sign and proceed through the intersection.
Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see cross traffic better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line or sign. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the road while looking.
